title: A Robot at the Restaurant
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a restaurant owner who introduced a serving robot. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a restaurant owner was struggling to find enough waiters for his busy lunch hour.
scenes: コマ1:レストランの男性店長が、ランチの混雑時に店員が足りず、料理を運ぶ店員が走り回っているのを見て困っている。
コマ2:「The next month」。店長が配膳ロボットの業者から説明を受けていて、ロボットが料理の皿を客席まで運んでいる。
コマ3:「A few weeks later」。客の子どもがロボットをスマートフォンで撮影して喜んでいる。厨房の店員たちは調理に集中している。
コマ4:「One evening」。閉店後、店長が、ロボットの導入で勤務時間を減らされたアルバイトの女子学生が、寂しそうに店を去るのを見送っている。
narrationSample: One day, a restaurant owner was struggling to find enough waiters for his busy lunch hour. Customers often had to wait a long time, and his staff were exhausted. The next month, he met with a company that sold serving robots, and he decided to try one. The robot carried plates of food from the kitchen to the tables without any trouble. A few weeks later, many customers were amused by it, and a child was taking pictures of it with a smartphone. The kitchen staff could focus on cooking, and the lunch service ran more smoothly. One evening, however, after the restaurant had closed, the owner watched a part-time student say goodbye. Her working hours had been cut because the robot was now doing much of her work.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the restaurant owner, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Efficiency matters, but I can't simply replace people. I should find other ways for that student to contribute, such as training her to manage the robots or helping with customer service."

questions.question: Do you think robots will replace many jobs in the service industry in the future?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think they will take over some jobs, especially repetitive tasks such as carrying food and taking orders. However, robots cannot offer the warm hospitality that customers value. So I think human workers will move toward roles that require communication and creativity.

questions.question: Should companies be required to retrain workers whose jobs are taken over by robots or AI?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I believe so. Workers did not choose to lose their jobs because of technological change, so companies that benefit from automation have a responsibility to help them. Government programs can support retraining, but companies should also offer new positions within the organization.

title: A Repair Café
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a woman whose smartphone broke. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a woman dropped her smartphone on the sidewalk, and the screen was badly cracked.
scenes: コマ1:女性が歩道でスマートフォンを落とし、画面がひび割れて途方に暮れている。
コマ2:「That afternoon」。女性が地域センターで開かれている「修理カフェ」で、ボランティアの男性に壊れた携帯電話を見せている。
コマ3:「The following Sunday」。女性が修理カフェで、ほかの参加者の古いラジオを直すのを手伝っていて、みんなが笑顔になっている。
コマ4:「A month later」。女性がごみ集積所で、まだ十分に使える新品同様のスマートフォンを男性が捨てようとしているのを見て、眉をひそめている。
narrationSample: One day, a woman dropped her smartphone on the sidewalk, and the screen was badly cracked. She was about to buy a new one when she noticed a poster for a repair café at the community center. That afternoon, she took her phone there, and a volunteer, a retired engineer, showed her how the screen could be replaced for a small fee. The following Sunday, she came back and helped other visitors fix old radios and toasters. A month later, however, she saw a man at the collection point throwing away a smartphone that looked almost new. She frowned, because she could not understand why he had discarded it so easily.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "That phone could have been used for several more years. I should explain that repairing it is cheaper and better for the environment. I could also invite him to the repair café."

questions.question: Do you think people in Japan throw away electronic products too quickly?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Many people replace their phones and computers every few years, mainly because they want the latest model, even when the old one still works. This creates a huge amount of electronic waste, which contains valuable metals that are hard to recover.

questions.question: Should manufacturers be required to make their products easier to repair?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I strongly believe so. If parts are easy to replace and repair manuals are available, people will be more willing to fix things instead of buying new ones. Some companies may argue that this raises costs, but the environmental benefits and the trust of customers would be worth it.

title: Tourists in an Old Town
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a man who ran a guesthouse in an old town. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One morning, a man who ran a guesthouse in an old town was woken up by noisy tourists outside his window.
scenes: コマ1:古い町並みで民宿を営む男性が、早朝に観光客の大声で目を覚まし、窓の外を見て顔をしかめている。
コマ2:「The next week」。男性が近所の住民たちと集まり、観光客のマナーについて話し合っている。住民の一人は「家の前で写真を撮らないで」と書いた看板を持っている。
コマ3:「A few months later」。男性が地元のガイドと一緒に、住民の生活道路を避けて、町の歴史を説明する散策ツアーを案内している。観光客が熱心に耳を傾けている。
コマ4:「That summer」。町の大通りは観光客であふれている。男性は、地元の年配の女性が人混みで地元の店に入れず、買い物をあきらめて帰るのを申し訳なさそうに見ている。
narrationSample: One morning, a man who ran a guesthouse in an old town was woken up by noisy tourists outside his window, and he was not happy about it. The next week, he met with his neighbors to discuss the problem. One of them had made a sign asking visitors not to take photos in front of people's homes. A few months later, the man started working with a local guide to offer a walking tour. The tour avoided residential alleys and explained the history of the town, and tourists listened eagerly. That summer, however, the main street was still crowded. He watched an elderly neighbor give up on buying vegetables at a local shop because she could not get through the crowd.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the man, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "Our guided tours are helping, but they can't solve everything. We need to work with the city to limit the number of tour buses and make sure residents can still shop in their own neighborhood."

questions.question: Do you think tourism has done more good than harm to Japanese cities?
questions.sampleAnswer: On balance, I think it has done more good than harm. Tourism brings income to local businesses and helps to preserve traditional buildings. However, when too many visitors arrive at the same time, residents lose their privacy and their daily lives become very difficult, so the benefits depend on how tourism is managed.

questions.question: Should governments limit the number of tourists who can visit popular places?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think limits are sometimes necessary. Popular places can be damaged by too many visitors, and residents deserve a peaceful life. However, the measures should be carefully designed, for example through reservation systems or higher fees during peak seasons, rather than simply banning visitors.

title: A Community Theater Play
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a retired teacher who directed a community theater play. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a retired teacher was asked to direct a play for the local community theater group.
scenes: コマ1:退職した元教師の女性が、地域の演劇サークルの稽古場で、台本を前に頭を抱えている。
コマ2:「A few weeks later」。主役の若い男性が、仕事が忙しくなったと言って稽古に来なくなり、女性がほかの団員と相談している。
コマ3:「The night before the performance」。団員たちが舞台の背景の絵を一緒に描いていて、夜遅くまで作業をしている。
コマ4:「On the opening night」。満席の公民館で観客が拍手を送っている。舞台の袖で女性が涙ぐんでいる。
narrationSample: One day, a retired teacher was asked to direct a play for the local community theater group. She had never directed anything before, and she was not sure she could do it. A few weeks later, the young man who was supposed to play the lead role stopped coming to rehearsals because his job had become busier. She talked with the other members, and together they found a solution. The night before the performance, the members stayed late to paint the background together. On the opening night, the community hall was full, and the audience gave a warm round of applause. The woman, standing at the side of the stage, was moved to tears.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I was worried that I couldn't lead them, but everyone's effort made this possible. I'm so grateful to each of them, and I should thank them personally after the show."

questions.question: Do you think schools should put more emphasis on arts education, such as drama and music?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I do. Drama and music help students build confidence, creativity, and the ability to work with others. These skills are valuable in any career, and they also help students express themselves in a world where communication matters so much.

questions.question: Should local governments spend more public money on cultural activities?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think they should, but the money must be spent wisely. Cultural activities enrich local life and can attract visitors, which benefits local businesses. However, governments should focus on programs that involve residents, rather than expensive events that only a small number of people attend.

title: A Night Shift at a Care Home
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a young woman who started working at a care home. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a young woman started working at a care home for elderly people.
scenes: コマ1:若い女性が夜勤の初日、介護施設の廊下で、ベテランの女性職員から仕事の説明を受けて緊張した顔をしている。
コマ2:「A few weeks later」。女性が夜勤を終えた後、疲れ切った様子で休憩室のソファに横になっている。
コマ3:「One night」。眠れずにいる高齢の男性入居者のそばに女性が座り、昔の歌を一緒に口ずさんでいる。男性が笑顔になっている。
コマ4:「The next morning」。施設の玄関で、女性が入居者の家族から感謝の手紙を受け取り、うれしさと今後への不安が入り混じった表情をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a young woman started working at a care home for elderly people. On her first night shift, an experienced staff member explained many tasks to her, and she felt nervous. A few weeks later, she was so exhausted after her shifts that she fell asleep on a sofa in the break room. One night, however, she noticed an elderly resident who could not sleep. She sat beside him and sang an old song that he remembered from his youth, and he smiled for the first time in days. The next morning, a family member handed her a thank-you letter at the entrance. She looked both happy and uncertain about her future.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the young woman, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm glad I could make a difference, but the work is so demanding. If I don't take care of my own health, I won't be able to keep helping others. Maybe I should talk to my supervisor about my schedule."

questions.question: Do you think the government should raise the salaries of care workers?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I think so. Care workers do physically and emotionally demanding work, yet their pay is much lower than in many other fields. Higher salaries would attract more people to the profession, which is important because Japan's population is aging rapidly.

questions.question: Should Japan accept more foreign workers to address the shortage of care workers?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think it should, but only if the government also improves working conditions and language training. Foreign workers can help fill the labor shortage, but if they are poorly supported, they may leave quickly. Helping them become part of the local community is also essential.

title: A Mock Job Interview
instruction: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a university student who was preparing for job interviews. You have two minutes to narrate the story.
firstSentence: One day, a university student received her fifth rejection letter from a company.
scenes: コマ1:大学4年の女子学生が、五通目の不採用通知のメールを見て、がっくりと肩を落としている。
コマ2:「The next week」。学生が大学のキャリアセンターで職員と模擬面接の練習をしている。職員が「もっと具体的な例を挙げましょう」と助言している。
コマ3:「A month later」。学生が企業の面接会場で、面接官に落ち着いて、ボランティア活動の経験を説明している。
コマ4:「That evening」。学生が内定の電話を受けて喜んでいる。しかし同じ面接を受けていた友人からのメッセージを読んで、複雑な表情をしている。
narrationSample: One day, a university student received her fifth rejection letter from a company, and she felt discouraged. The next week, she went to the career center at her university and practiced mock job interviews with a staff member. The staff member advised her to give concrete examples instead of general statements. A month later, she was calmly explaining her experience leading a volunteer project during an interview at a company. That evening, she received a call offering her a job, and she was delighted. However, when she read a message from a friend who had been interviewing for the same job, she looked troubled.

questions.question: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were the student, what would you be thinking?
questions.sampleAnswer: I'd be thinking, "I'm happy to have the offer, but I shouldn't feel guilty about it. My friend is just as capable, and I was simply fortunate this time. I'll ask how she is doing and offer to help her prepare for her next interview."

questions.question: Do you think job interviews are a good way to judge whether a person will be a good employee?
questions.sampleAnswer: I think they are useful but not perfect. Interviews show a person's communication skills and attitude, which matter a great deal in the workplace. However, some people perform well in interviews but lack the skills needed for the actual job, so companies should also consider internships or trial work.

questions.question: Should Japanese companies hire more mid-career workers instead of mainly recruiting new graduates?
questions.sampleAnswer: Yes, I believe they should. Mid-career workers bring practical experience and different perspectives that can help companies innovate. Companies that rely only on new graduates may lack the skills needed to compete in a rapidly changing global market. However, they also need to provide training so that these workers can adapt to new roles.
